## HEADNOTE
Sample Tenancy Act, 2001, Section 15 - subletting without the landlord's written consent is a ground for eviction; consent cannot be inferred from acceptance of rent alone.
## FACTS
The tenant allowed a third party to run a business from part of the premises. The landlord continued to accept rent from the tenant for two years and then sought eviction.
## ARGUMENTS
The tenant argued that the landlord's acceptance of rent amounted to implied consent. The landlord relied on the requirement of written consent in Section 15.
## REASONING
Section 15 requires the landlord's written consent to any subletting. Acceptance of rent from the tenant is consistent with the tenancy continuing and says nothing about the sub-tenant. Implied consent would defeat the requirement of writing.
## HOLDING
Subletting without written consent entitles the landlord to eviction under Section 15. Acceptance of rent does not amount to consent.
